summary:
The name of this Act is the Appropriation Act, 2083 (Section 1, Subsection 1, Page 1). This Act shall come into force on 1 Sawan 2083 (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 1). The main purpose of this Act is to grant authority to appropriate and spend amounts from the Federal Consolidated Fund for the services and functions of the financial year 2083/84 (Preamble, Page 1; Section 3, Page 2). Under this Act, for the services and functions other than items charged on the Federal Consolidated Fund for the financial year 2083/84, spending may be made from the Federal Consolidated Fund up to Rs. 17,06,03,24,00,000, including current expenditure, capital expenditure, and financial management (Section 2, Page 1-2).

Notwithstanding anything contained in prevailing law, the spending authority for the appropriated amount for the financial year 2083/84 shall belong to the authorized officer starting from the date of commencement of this Act (Section 4, Subsection 1, Page 2). Based on that authority, the Treasury and Accounts Controller Office shall release the allocated amount to the concerned body (Section 4, Subsection 2, Page 2). Programs included in the Ministry Budget Information System shall be considered approved programs for budget execution (Section 4, Subsection 5, Page 3). The Ministry of Finance may transfer budget up to 10 percent of the total allocated amount from one grant code to another or transfer sources (Section 5, Subsections 1 and 2, Page 3). Any amount may be viremented within budget sub-heads of the same grant code (Section 5, Subsection 2, Clause a, Page 3). Amounts allocated under capital expenditure cannot be viremented to current expenditure except for financial investment and principal and interest payments on debt (Section 5, Subsection 2, Clause b, Page 3). Amounts allocated under financial management cannot be viremented to current expenditure except for principal and interest payments, and amounts allocated for principal repayments cannot be viremented anywhere except interest payments (Section 5, Subsection 2, Clause c, Page 3-4). Financial equalization grants allocated under grant codes 701 and 801 for provincial or local levels shall not be viremented to other grant codes (Section 5, Subsection 3, Page 4). The responsible accounting officer may vire current and capital expenditure titles within the same grant code, amend activities, amend inter-economic codes for specified expenditure titles, and make quarterly revisions of approved annual programs (Section 5, Subsections 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9, Pages 5-6). Approval of the Ministry of Finance is required if the source changes during such virement or revision (Section 5, Subsection 10, Page 6). Amounts under grant code 701 shall be deposited into the Provincial Consolidated Fund and amounts under grant code 801 into the Local Consolidated Fund (Section 6, Subsections 1 and 2, Page 8). The Financial Comptroller General Office shall transfer financial equalization grants in four installments on 2 Bhadra 2083, 2 Kartik 2083, 2 Magh 2083, and 2 Baishakh 2084 (Section 6, Subsection 3, Page 8). The first and second installments shall be transferred based on initial estimates, the third installment based on the revenue collection ratio up to end of Poush, and the fourth installment based on the revenue collection ratio up to end of Chaitra (Section 6, Subsection 4, Page 8). The Financial Comptroller General Office shall transfer one-third of conditional grants to provincial or local consolidated funds by 2 Bhadra 2083 (Section 6, Subsection 5, Page 8). Provincial or local levels must submit workplans, monthly cash flow details, and approved revenue and expenditure estimates to the concerned Treasury and Accounts Controller Office by end of Sawan (Section 6, Subsection 6, Page 9). Provincial or local levels must submit physical progress and expenditure details by 15 Mangsir 2083, 15 Chaitra 2083, and 15 Ashadh 2084, and annual financial statements by end of Sawan 2084 (Section 6, Subsection 7, Page 9). The Financial Comptroller General Office shall transfer remaining conditional grant reimbursements by 25 Mangsir 2083, 25 Chaitra 2083, and 20 Ashadh 2084 (Section 6, Subsection 8, Page 9-10). Unspent balances of conditional, complementary, and special grants must be returned to the Federal Consolidated Fund through the Treasury and Accounts Controller Office by end of Ashadh of the same financial year (Section 6, Subsection 10, Page 10). The ministry may decide to implement federal projects through provincial or local levels, and such released amounts cannot be recorded as revenue in provincial or local consolidated funds (Section 7, Subsections 1, 4, 5 and 6, Pages 10-11). Provincial or local levels may execute capital projects through federal offices, and unspent balances of local projects must be returned to the Local Consolidated Fund at the end of the financial year (Section 7, Subsections 2 and 8, Pages 11-12). Prior to implementing infrastructure projects included in the Ministry Budget Information System, Project Bank entry procedures must be completed (Section 7, Subsection 12, Page 13). Construction of buildings from allocated funds must be done on government land (Section 7, Subsection 13, Page 14). Provincial or local levels must spend collected revenue and financial transfers by framing laws following federal economic policies, depositing all income into consolidated funds, spending grants for designated purposes, not transferring capital funds to current expenditure, formulating balanced budgets within the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework, and implementing specified accounting and reporting systems (Section 9, Subsections 1 and 2, Pages 15-16). Prior consent of the Ministry of Finance must be obtained before making decisions that create financial liabilities outside the budget (Section 9, Subsection 7, Page 17).
